name: Blast phase

lead: In blast-and-cruise language, the blast phase is the period of deliberately higher intake of anabolic compounds, followed by a lower-intake cruise phase. Users describe it as the stretch in which they push for more muscle, a fuller physique and a more athletic look.

Anabolic steroids are a prescription drug class, and medical use is for conditions such as low testosterone. The effects of supraphysiologic use, including cardiovascular changes, liver effects with oral forms, acne, gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, reduced sperm production and mood changes, are documented.

paras: Within the community the pattern alternates a higher-intake blast with a lower-intake cruise, with the blast tied to a growth or bulking goal. Details of compounds and amounts are not given here.

Documented adverse effects include raised LDL and lowered HDL cholesterol, left ventricular hypertrophy, liver damage (mainly with oral compounds), acne, gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, reduced sperm production and mood or aggression changes. Dependence has been reported in long-term supraphysiologic users. These are prescription-only substances in many countries.

angle.text: Users describe the blast as the growth-focused period of a longer pattern, intended to add muscle and size. The same compounds are associated with documented harms.

lead: In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities, the blast phase is the higher-intake half of a blast-and-cruise pattern. Users aim it at adding muscle and size, which they connect to a more developed physique.[1] The term should not be confused with the "blast phase" of leukemia and myeloproliferative diseases, an unrelated medical use.[2]

Anabolic steroids are medically used to treat conditions such as late-onset hypogonadism.[3] Wikipedia's anabolic steroid article reports that supraphysiologic use is associated with cardiovascular, hepatic, dermatologic, reproductive and psychological adverse effects, and that dependence has been seen in weightlifters and bodybuilders who chronically took high doses.[3]

paras: The blast is the period of higher intake in the blast-and-cruise pattern, as users describe it, followed by a lower-intake cruise.[1] This wiki does not document compounds, amounts or schedules.

The Wikipedia anabolic steroid article lists raised LDL and lower HDL cholesterol, left ventricular hypertrophy, liver damage mainly with oral forms, acne, gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, reduced sperm production, and mood and aggression changes.[3] It also notes that clomifene and hCG usually restore normal testosterone production after a short course of one to two months.[3]
No studies found on the blast phase as a pattern. The unrelated clinical term in leukemia and myelofibrosis is covered in hematology reviews.[2]
